## A Metal Design Language

The overarching theme of the Lab is to develop a bioinorganic programming language in which topological self-assembly of nucleic acids is carried out using metal base pairs. By replacing select hydrogen bonds with metal coordination bonds, we aim to expand the intrinsic functionality of nucleic acids to interface with light, electrons, and biochemical inputs.

Using high-throughput X-ray crystallography, iterative design, and collaboration with chemists and physicists, we aim to make molecules, such as the 3D tile shown here, possible in the near future.
